page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m8.8xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance operating on KVM virtualization. The system is provisioned with 32 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Accompanied by 256.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, aligning it with memory-intensive server architectures requiring high capacity per execution thread.

The hardware profile contains zero local storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize network-attached cloud storage services. Baseline network performance is configured at 16 Gbps, facilitating rapid data movement across cluster topologies or between remote block storage endpoints. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units or hardware coprocessors.

In terms of resource efficiency, the 1:8 compute-to-memory balance enables high-capacity caching and stateful execution without over-provisioning processing cores. Tradeoffs involve reliance on remote networking for all persistent disk IO and the absence of specialized accelerators. The instance configuration is well aligned with in-memory caching solutions, large relational or NoSQL databases, memory-bound enterprise applications, and medium-scale ETL pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m8.8xlarge is an x86_64 instance built on KVM virtualization, featuring 32 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs operating at 2.7 GHz and 256.0 GB of memory. Configured with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio yielding 8.0 GB per core, the system prioritizes memory density over compute scaling. It provisions a 16 Gbps baseline network interface to manage high-throughput data traffic, while including zero local storage and no hardware accelerators. Storage architecture relies entirely on external network-attached volumes. By providing dedicated core allocation alongside substantial memory capacity, the instance eliminates hypervisor contention for high-footprint workloads. These characteristics make the ecs.u2i-c1m8.8xlarge suitable for in-memory databases, distributed caching systems, large batch ETL operations, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
